identity.title: Cullin-5 RING E3 ligase limits CD8(+) T-cell persistence and effector responses during chronic antigen stimulation.

content.abstract: T-cell exhaustion limits durable antitumor responses and remains a barrier to adoptive cell therapies (ACT) in solid tumors. To identify regulators of T-cell persistence, we performed genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens in primary human CD8(+) T cells expressing an NY-ESO-1-specific T-cell receptor and subjected them to repeated tumor cell rechallenge. These screens revealed enrichment of single-guide RNAs targeting components of Cullin-RING E3 ligases, particularly Cullin-5 (CRL5) assemblies comprising CUL5, RNF7, and ARIH2. Disruption of CRL5 genes in T cells preserved cytotoxic activity and enhanced cytokine production while sustaining effector-associated transcriptional programs and suppressing exhaustion-related signatures. Pharmacologic inhibition of cullin neddylation with the NEDD8-activating enzyme inhibitor MLN4924 recapitulated CRL5 loss and enhanced T-cell effector function in vitro. In a human melanoma xenograft model, ACT with CRL5-deficient T cells improved tumor control. Together, these findings identify CRL5 as a negative regulator of T-cell fitness and a potential therapeutic target to enhance ACT durability in solid tumors.
